                                    PROSECUTION SUMMARY

                        Office of Rail and Road v Network Rail Infrastructure Limited

Court:                           Bristol Crown Court

Sentencing date:                 4 April 2012

Defendant:                       Network Rail Infrastructure Limited

Incident date:                   28 June 2010

Location:                        Grayrigg, Cumbria

Plea:                            Guilty

Offences:

Section 3(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974 - Failure to conduct its
undertaking in such a way as to ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, that persons
not in its employment who may be affected thereby are not thereby exposed to risks to
their health or safety.

Sentence:

Fine: £4,000,000
Costs: £215,000

Total: £4,215,000

Details of the case:

On 23 February 2007, Virgin West Coast Pendolino train 1S83 derailed at Grayrigg, Cumbria
whilst travelling at 95mph. The train struck a set of points which had become displaced due
to the failure of components within the points mechanism. As a consequence of the derailment,
one passenger, Margaret Masson (aged 84), died from her injuries. A further 88 passengers
and staff were injured, of which 28 were seriously injured.

The Office of Rail and Road's investigation found that Network Rail had failed to implement
adequate inspection and maintenance regimes for the points at Grayrigg. The stretcher bars
that hold the rails in position had become worn and eventually broke, allowing the rails to
move out of alignment.

Network Rail accepted responsibility for the failures that led to the derailment and
entered a guilty plea.

The judge noted that Network Rail had taken steps to improve its maintenance procedures
following the incident and had cooperated fully with the investigation.
